prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1488; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reports a collision at an intersection while the other driver was turning left across her path. She states she was proceeding straight on a green signal. Initial contact appears to be front quarter panel of the insured vehicle to rear passenger door of the claimant's vehicle. Scene photos requested.

Entry 2: Claimant called to report ongoing right shoulder pain following the collision and says she was evaluated at an urgent care facility. Shoulder injury reported. Claimant has not retained an attorney and says she is handling the claim directly. Advised her of the process for submitting medical records and repair estimates.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer noted the insured driver stated he did not see the claimant's vehicle before beginning the left turn. Witness statement from a pedestrian at the corner supports the claimant's account of the signal phase. Liability appears to lean toward the insured driver, pending further review.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant regarding medical documentation. She has provided urgent care discharge notes describing a shoulder strain with limited range of motion and a recommendation for physical therapy. Requested the treatment plan and any imaging results. Claimant asked when the property damage would be addressed; explained the appraisal is scheduled and her vehicle is at the designated repair shop.

Entry 5: Received repair estimate for the claimant's vehicle and the independent appraisal report. Claimant confirmed she has started physical therapy and expects to continue for several weeks. Bodily injury evaluation remains open while treatment is ongoing. Will follow up on the physical therapy progress notes and reassess once a treatment summary is available.
